title: Models of complex systems should first be judged by comparing overall pictures

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Models of complex systems should first be judged by comparing overall pictures

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: For systems with complex behavior, a model cannot be adequately assessed by matching a few extracted numbers; the best first test is a visual comparison of the model's overall behavior with that of the real system.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: by far the best first step in assessing a model is not to look at numbers or other details, but rather just to use one's eyes, and to compare overall pictures of a system with pictures from the model.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 8, “Implications for Everyday Systems”; section “Issues of Modelling” (from p. 363), p. 365. Scope: scientific modelling of systems with complex behavior

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch08-01: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.15

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim recommends a modelling practice rather than specifying a measurable consequence. Empirical studies of evaluator performance would depend on chosen tasks, losses, and observers and could not establish visual comparison as generally best. Operationalization would materially reinterpret the statement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The statement could be reframed as a comparison of how well human visual ratings and numerical summaries predict held-out model failures, but that would test a chosen evaluation workflow rather than the asserted normative best first step.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Best first test is normative and task-dependent.

Overall picture and adequate assessment have no invariant decision criteria.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.12
operationalizability: 0.18
data existence: 0.15
data adequacy: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.2

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is a prescription for scientific practice. Any later success or failure of a model can be reconciled with having looked at pictures first or at numbers first, because the claim does not fix what the pictures or the numbers must predict. No public dataset supplies a decision criterion that would settle it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The recommendation that visual comparison is the best first assessment of a complex model does not name a measured variable or a result that would confirm or refute it independently of a prior judgment about what counts as an adequate test.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Best and adequately assessed are methodological judgments, not outcomes that distinguish the recommendation from rival standards of model testing.
